Description: Move await into branches where actually used to avoid blocking unused case-loading paths
Do: Move await operations into branches where they're needed
Don't: Await at top of function blocking all branches
Code Example Good: if (skip) return { skipped: true }; const matter = await fetchMatter()
Code Example Bad: const matter = await fetchMatter(); if (skip) return { skipped: true }

Description: Fetch independent client and matter data concurrently using Promise.all()
Code Example Bad: const client = await fetchClient(); const matters = await fetchMatters()

Description: Use better-all for case data with partial dependencies to maximize parallelism
Do: Use better-all to start each task at earliest possible moment
Don't: Wait for unrelated data before starting dependent fetch
Code Example Good: await all({ client() {}, config() {}, matters() { return fetch((await this.$.client).id) } })
Code Example Bad: const [client, config] = await Promise.all([...]); const matters = await fetchMatters(client.id)

Description: In case-management API routes start independent operations immediately even if not awaited yet
Do: Start promises early and await late
Code Example Good: const sessionP = auth(); const firmP = fetchFirm(); const session = await sessionP
Code Example Bad: const session = await auth(); const firm = await fetchFirm()

Description: Use Suspense to show the case-dashboard shell faster while data loads
Do: Wrap async components in Suspense boundaries
Don't: Await data blocking entire page render
Code Example Bad: const cases = await fetchCases(); return <CaseList data={cases} />

Description: Import directly from source files to avoid loading unused modules in the portal
Use next/dynamic to lazy-load the heavy document viewer not needed on initial render
Don't: Import heavy components at top level
Code Example Good: const DocViewer = dynamic(() => import('./doc-viewer'), { ssr: false })

Description: Load analytics and logging after hydration since they don't block portal interaction
Code Example Good: const Analytics = dynamic(() => import('@vercel/analytics'), { ssr: false })

Description: Load the large e-filing module only when a client starts a filing
Preload the document viewer on hover before the attorney opens a file
Use React.cache() to dedupe client lookups within a single request
Don't: Fetch same data multiple times in tree
Code Example Good: export const getClient = cache(async () => await db.client.find())
Code Example Bad: export async function getClient() { return await db.client.find() }

Description: Use LRU cache for practice-area data shared across sequential requests
Don't: Refetch same data on every request
Code Example Good: const cache = new LRUCache({ max: 1000, ttl: 5*60*1000 })

Description: Only pass client fields actually used across RSC boundaries (avoid leaking privileged data)
Do: Pass only needed fields to client components

Description: Restructure the case dashboard to parallelize data fetching in RSC
Do: Use component composition for parallel fetches

Description: Use Next.js after() to log an audit trail after the response is sent
Use SWR for automatic request dedup and caching of the matter list
Do: Use useSWR for client data fetching

Description: Share global event listeners across document-review component instances
Don't subscribe to search params only used in a case-filter callback
Don't: Subscribe to state used only in handlers
Code Example Good: const handleFilter = () => { const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search) }
Code Example Bad: const params = useSearchParams(); const handleFilter = () => { params.get('practiceArea') }

Description: Extract expensive attorney-avatar work into memoized components for early returns
Don't: Compute expensive values before early return
Code Example Good: const AttorneyAvatar = memo(({ attorney }) => ...); if (loading) return <Skeleton />
Code Example Bad: const avatar = useMemo(() => compute(attorney)); if (loading) return <Skeleton />

Description: Specify primitive dependencies instead of the whole client object in effects
Do: Use primitive values in dependency arrays

Description: Subscribe to a derived boolean instead of continuous width in the responsive case view
Code Example Bad: const width = useWindowWidth(); const isMobile = width < 768

Description: Use functional setState when appending documents to a matter for stable callbacks
Pass a function to useState for an expensive legal-research index
Do: Use function form for expensive init

Description: Mark frequent non-urgent updates on a long document scroll as transitions
Don't: Block UI on every state change

Description: Wrap the firm-logo SVG in a div and animate the wrapper for hardware acceleration
Apply content-visibility: auto to defer off-screen e-discovery rows
Extract the static case-card skeleton outside components to avoid re-creation
Do: Hoist static elements to module scope
Code Example Good: const skeleton = <div class='animate-pulse' />; function C() { return skeleton }

Description: Use an inline script to set the client's saved portal theme before hydration
Do: Inject sync script for client-only values

Description: Use a ternary instead of && when an unread-message count can be 0
Use Activity to preserve the case-filters panel state when toggled
Do: Use Activity for expensive toggle components

Description: Group CSS changes when highlighting a matched e-discovery term to minimize reflows
Don't: Change styles one property at a time

Description: Build a Map for repeated client lookups instead of multiple .find() calls
Do: Build index Map for O(1) lookups
Code Example Good: const byId = new Map(clients.map(c => [c.id, c])); byId.get(id)
Code Example Bad: clients.find(c => c.id === matter.clientId) // O(n) each time

Description: Cache nested config lookups in hot billing-calculation paths
Use a module-level Map to cache repeated matter-slug generation
Do: Use Map cache for repeated calls
Code Example Good: const cache = new Map(); if (cache.has(x)) return cache.get(x)

Description: Cache localStorage reads of the portal theme in memory
Combine multiple filter/map passes when categorizing matters into one loop
Code Example Good: for (m of matters) { if (m.isOpen) open.push(m); if (m.isOverdue) overdue.push(m) }

Description: Check array lengths before expensively comparing two document sets
Code Example Good: if (a.length !== b.length) return true; // then compare
Code Example Bad: a.sort().join() !== b.sort().join() // even when lengths differ

Description: Return early on the first invalid field when validating a client intake
Don't: Process all items then check errors
Code Example Good: for (c of clients) { if (!c.email) return { error: 'Email required' } }
Code Example Bad: let hasError; for (...) { if (!email) hasError=true }; if (hasError)...

Description: Don't create the case-number RegExp inside render - hoist or memoize
Code Example Bad: function C() { const re = new RegExp(pattern); re.test(x) }

Description: Use a loop to find the earliest filing deadline instead of sort - O(n) vs O(n log n)
Code Example Good: let earliest = dates[0]; for (d of dates) if (d < earliest) earliest = d

Description: Use a Set for O(1) checks of allowed practice-area codes instead of includes()
Do: Convert to Set for membership checks

Description: Use toSorted() to order the attorney directory without mutating the source array
Store the case-update callback in a ref for a stable websocket subscription
Access the latest intake callback without adding it to dependency arrays
Do: Use useLatest for fresh values in stable callbacks
Code Example Good: const cbRef = useLatest(cb); useEffect(() => { setTimeout(() => cbRef.current()) }, [])
